newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan general quits for criticising war policy.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan general quits for criticising war policy.

text.p: A Ugandan army general has resigned after criticising President Yoweri Museveni's war strategy and calling army commanders incompetent thieves.

Major-General David Tinyefunza quit his position as senior military adviser to Museveni on Wednesday after the army's high command summoned him for breaking ranks with military protocol, official sources said on Thursday.

In testimony to a parliamentary committee, obtained by Reuters on Thursday, Tinyefunza criticised the conduct of the war against the Christian fundamentalist Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) in the north.
The LRA, led by Joseph Kony, has been fighting the army in the Gulu and other northern districts since 1987.

"Now the president is in Gulu in sandbags. If all these big commanders can't fight Kony and it requires Museveni to go into sandbags...this country is in trouble. It shows there is something basically wrong with this country," Tinyefunza said.
Asked why the war had gone on so long, Tinyefunza replied: "There was mishandling. The war is taking long because soldiers are not fighting. Soldiers are tired, they have low morale."

"Some of these commanders are thieves. How can a thief command soldiers? An army does not operate by crisis like you see it here...People who know what to do must be put in charge and corruption must be fought," Tinyefunza added.
The general said people dying in the north were from all Uganda's tribes and the government had failed to end the endemic poverty.
"If you go to that area, you can't imagine that it is part of Uganda. If you do not end a war in 11 years and your people are dying, are you worth being a government?" he asked.
The committee is holding hearings on Ugandan wars and Tinyefunza appeared before it this week, a member said.
The army commander, Major-General Mugisha Muntu, told the same committee this week the LRA was the most serious threat so far to the internal security of Uganda.
Museveni, in Gulu to direct the war, has said he is determined to defeat Joseph Kony militarily.

Tinyefunza, one of only three major-generals in the Ugandan army, had a prominent part in Museveni's guerrilla war against the previous government in the early 1980s. After the guerrillas came to power, he commanded the army in the north for some years but was later recalled to Kampala.
